title: Azure Policy Compliance and Non-Compliant Resources

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `mscs:azure:audit` events with `resourceId=*Microsoft.Authorization/policyAssignments*` into `index=azure`. Confirm UC-4.2.27 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `mscs:azure:audit` traffic without `resourceId=*Microsoft.Authorization/policyAssignments*`. Confirm UC-4.2.27 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=azure` sourcetype=`mscs:azure:audit` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.

description: UC-4.2.27 — Azure Policy Compliance and Non-Compliant Resources: queries Microsoft Azure `mscs:azure:audit` for search criteria `resourceId=*Microsoft.Authorization/policyAssignments*` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On Microsoft Azure, detecting 'Azure Policy Compliance and Non-Compliant Resources' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.2.27 drives medium-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Use Azure Policy compliance API or export policy states to storage/Event Hub. Ingest in Splunk. Dashboard compliance % by policy and resource group. Alert when critical policy becomes non-compliant.
visualization: Table (policy, resource, state), Pie chart (compliant %), Bar chart (non-compliant by type).

| tstats `summariesonly` count

dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Change (All_Changes).
knownFalsePositives: Our own break-glass and automation accounts show up the same as anyone else, and a delete or write during a change window is expected. We allowlist the roles that do routine maintenance and we link alerts to approved changes before we call an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` with the modular input for `mscs:azure:audit`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Use Azure Policy compliance API or export policy states to storage/Event Hub. Ingest in Splunk. Dashboard compliance % by policy and resource group. Alert when critical policy becomes non-compliant.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:audit" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:audit" resourceId=*Microsoft.Authorization/policyAssignments*
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.27_azure_policy_compliance_27"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `mscs:azure:audit` in `index=azure` to detect azure policy compliance and non-compliant resources. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_27_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Table (policy, resource, state), Pie chart (compliant %), Bar chart (non-compliant by type)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of azure policy compliance and non-compliant resources so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
